key_insight: Federated learning can potentially match centralised performance for personalised breast cancer progression prediction while keeping patient data local.
clinical_relevance: This could help support privacy-preserving, institution-spanning models for personalised treatment planning in breast cancer care.
method: Multimodal federated learning used clinical, tumour, biomarker, demographic, and MRI data.
Modelled changes in tumour characteristics over time and compared federated vs centralised training.
Assessed transparency, scalability, security, and fairness for real-world deployment.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a comparative evaluation of federated learning against a centralised model on aggregated multimodal breast cancer data, focusing on predictive performance and deployment readiness.
watch_item: Real-world use may depend on strong cross-site coordination, secure update handling, and careful monitoring of subgroup performance and fairness.
paper_title: Trustworthy Privacy-Preserving Multimodal Federated Learning for Personalised Breast Cancer Prediction
